title: kate-ui: start a language server for the open document
summary: The window reads lsp/settings.json under the application support directory, or a built-in default with rust-analyzer and clangd, picks the server for the document's syntax definition name, spawns and initializes it once per server name, and sends didOpen, didChange from drain_changes, and didClose. Events are polled on a timer.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. session.rs imports GPUI, the crate builds only on macOS, and the owner looks at the window after the change.

definitions.definition:
/// Server settings: the user file when it parses, else the built-in defaults.
fn server_settings(home: Option<&std::path::Path>) -> kate_lsp::ServersConfig

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: Create crates/kate-ui/lsp-defaults.json with servers rust (rust-analyzer, ^Rust$) and c (clangd, ^(C|ANSI C89|C\\+\\+)$) and include it with include_str. server_settings reads home/Library/Application Support/KateM5Rust/lsp/settings.json; a missing or bad file falls back to the defaults. When a document with a path and a definition opens, server_for_mode picks a server; spawn and initialize it in a background thread with a 10 second timeout when it is not running; then did_open with the definition name lowercased as language id and version 1. After every run_command and file request, drain_changes and send did_change with content_changes for documents that have a server, raising the version. A GPUI timer every 100 ms polls each client and stores Diagnostics events per document for the next packet. did_close when the last view of the document closes. A spawn failure shows one notice sentence and does not retry. The test server_settings_falls_back_to_the_defaults asserts server_settings(None) has a rust server with command [rust-analyzer]. The owner opens a Rust file with rust-analyzer installed and sees no error. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: session::tests::server_settings_falls_back_to_the_defaults
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because server_settings does not exist. After the change the built-in defaults name rust-analyzer when no user file exists.
